rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to spread a wide range of hydrophobicities while keeping most compounds likely to elute within the 42 min window. This gives an informative first map of retention coverage, selectivity, and whether the sample needs a weaker/stronger gradient or temperature shift next.

All 10 compounds eluted with perfect resolution, so the only improvement available is reducing runtime. Lowering phi1 while keeping phi0, tG, and T fixed should retain the same early-gradient selectivity but slow the stronger late elution enough to test whether we can preserve baseline separation while improving the time term.

The first run already had full resolution, so we should now compress the method rather than weaken it. Shortening the gradient at the successful composition range should pull the last peak earlier and improve the time term while likely keeping all separations safely above the resolution threshold.

Injection 3 is nearly optimal on time, but one pair fell just below 1.5 resolution. A small increase in gradient time from 14 to 16 min should selectively ease that compression and recover full resolution while keeping the run short enough to stay near the top CRF.

The optimum appears to sit near tG 14 min, limited only by the 6/7 pair. A small temperature decrease may change selectivity enough to open that pair while preserving the very short elution window that gave the near-maximal CRF.

Lower temperature worsened selectivity by creating a new critical pair, so test the opposite direction while keeping the highly favorable fast gradient. A modest increase to 45 C may improve selectivity around the compressed middle cluster and preserve the zero time penalty.

Temperature changes worsened the critical cluster, so probe selectivity with a weaker starting composition while keeping the near-optimal fast gradient. Lowering phi0 should expand early-to-mid retention spacing and may lift the 6/7 pair above 1.5 without introducing a time penalty.

The best region remains the 14 min, 40 C method, with only the 6/7 pair slightly under-resolved. Increasing phi1 may alter the late-gradient slope/selectivity enough to open that pair while keeping all compounds within the no-time-penalty window.

Raising phi1 compressed the critical pair further, so move in the opposite direction with a slightly shallower gradient while staying in the zero-time-penalty region. This should test whether a modest reduction in gradient strength can push the 6/7 pair over 1.5 without sacrificing the otherwise excellent fast separation.

Since 0.10 to 0.85 at 14 min and 40 C already gives the maximum CRF, the only useful follow-up is a nearby confirmatory perturbation to map robustness around the optimum. Increasing phi0 slightly tests whether the separation remains perfect with a steeper effective gradient and even earlier elution, while staying close to the best conditions.

You already have two distinct methods at the maximum CRF, so the best use of another run is to expand the robust optimum region. Increasing phi0 one more step tests whether the method can be made still stronger and faster at the front end while preserving complete resolution and zero time penalty.

The optimum seems to lie near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 around 0.85, with higher phi0 starting to compress the critical pair. Lowering phi1 one step from the successful 0.15/0.85 condition may slightly relax the mid-gradient crowding and preserve the maximum CRF region.

You have already established a broad optimum plateau, and the best two methods cluster at phi0 0.10–0.15 with phi1 0.85. Testing phi1 0.90 at the successful phi0 0.15 point maps the opposite side of that plateau and checks whether selectivity remains perfect with slightly stronger late elution.

The maximum-CRF region is centered on phi1 0.85, and lower phi0 previously moved retention later with only a slight resolution loss at phi1 0.90. Combining the successful phi1 0.85 with the lower phi0 tests whether that extra early retention improves or maintains the critical 6/7 spacing while staying in the zero-time-penalty window.

You have already reached the maximum CRF, so the only worthwhile exploration is to see whether a still shorter gradient can preserve full resolution. Since 14 min at 0.10/0.85 has comfortable margin on the critical pair, a 12 min test probes the lower tG boundary of the optimum plateau.

At 14 min, both phi0 0.10 and 0.15 gave CRF 1.000, and phi0 0.15 kept the critical pair nearly as open as phi0 0.10. Testing the shorter 12 min gradient at phi0 0.15 checks whether this slightly stronger start better preserves the 6/7 resolution when the gradient is compressed.

The optimum at 14 min is broad in composition but sensitive to temperature, and only 35 C and 45 C were tested at phi1 0.90 where selectivity worsened. Rechecking 35 C at the best phi1 0.85 condition tests whether the shallower successful gradient reshapes the critical 6/7 pair enough to retain a maximum-CRF method at a lower temperature.

The best composition has been found, and temperature is the remaining untested axis at that exact optimum. Running 45 C at phi0 0.10, phi1 0.85, tG 14 completes the local map and confirms whether the strong temperature sensitivity seen at phi1 0.90 persists at the best phi1.

With the optimum composition established, a slightly longer gradient at the second max-CRF composition probes robustness in tG and should further open the critical pair. This maps whether the perfect-score region extends upward in tG around phi0 0.15, phi1 0.85.

At 14 min, phi0 0.15 and phi1 0.80 gave the widest margin on the critical pair but just missed a perfect score because of slightly longer retention. Testing the shorter 12 min gradient at that composition explores whether some of the extra resolution margin can be traded for speed while staying fully resolved.

The two perfect methods and nearby results suggest a ridge around phi1 0.80–0.85 and phi0 0.10–0.15 at 14 min, but phi0 0.10 with phi1 0.80 has not yet been tested. This fills that remaining hole in the local optimum map and checks whether the best score plateau extends to the lower phi0 edge at the shallower gradient.

The best methods are both at 40 C, but only phi0 0.10/phi1 0.85 has been checked at 45 C and it degraded badly. Testing 45 C at the other perfect-score composition, phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85, completes the local robustness map and verifies whether that slightly higher phi0 is any less temperature-sensitive.

With 45 C strongly degrading the critical pair, the remaining untested neighbor around the two perfect methods is 35 C at phi0 0.15/phi1 0.85. This final temperature check completes the local optimum map and confirms whether both perfect-score methods share the same sharp temperature dependence.

You already have the maximum score, so the remaining value is just to finish mapping the 40 C neighborhood around the optimum. This untested corner combines the lower phi0 with the shallower successful phi1 and could show whether the perfect-score plateau extends diagonally across the local design space.

For the final shot, fill the last obvious 40 C neighbor near the optimum ridge by combining higher phi0 with the shallower phi1 0.80. This checks whether the perfect-score plateau is bounded mainly by excessive phi0 or by phi1, while staying close enough to the proven best region to remain informative.
